ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the cross-section of a certain dam of a reservoir is a trapezoid $ABCD$, with the height of the dam $DE = 5m$, and the slope ratio of slope $BC$ is $5\colon 12$. What is the length of slope $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, draw line CF$\perp$AB through point C, with F being the foot of the perpendicular. Thus,\\
$\because$ Dam height $DE=5m$, and CF$\perp$AB,\\
$\therefore$DE=CF=5cm\\
Moreover, the slope ratio of slope $BC$ is $5:12$\\
$\therefore$BF=12cm,\\
In $\triangle BCF$\\
$BC= \sqrt{CF^{2}+BF^{2}}$\\
$= \sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}}$\\
$=\boxed{13}$cm

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a trapezoid ABCD, AB is the lower base, DC is above and approximately parallel to AB; D is at the upper left, C is at the upper right, and BC is the right-side slope; from D, a dashed perpendicular line is drawn to AB, with the foot of the perpendicular being E, indicating the dam height DE=5 m. Reasoning: According to the specified method, draw a perpendicular from C to AB, with the foot of the perpendicular being F. Because C and D are both on the upper base DC, which is parallel to AB, the perpendicular distance from C to AB is equal to the perpendicular distance from D to AB, namely CF=DE=5 m. The slope ratio of slope BC is 5:12, indicating that the ratio of vertical height to horizontal distance is 5:12; when the vertical leg CF=5 m, the horizontal leg BF=12 m. In right triangle BCF, by the Pythagorean theorem, BC=sqrt(CF^2+BF^2)=sqrt(5^2+12^2)=sqrt(169)=13 m.
